m: Çankırı Province (Turkish: Çankırı ili) is a province of Turkey, which lies close to the capital, Ankara. The provincial capital is Çankırı. Its area is 7,542 km2, and its population is 195,766 (2022).

Q15256839: The Mount Ilgaz National Park (Turkish: Ilgaz Dağı Milli Parkı) is a protected area established on June 2, 1976 and located on the Ilgaz Mountains at the borderline between Kastamonu Province and Çankırı Province in the western Black Sea Region of Turkey. Natural resources and its potential for recreational activities are the main values of the national park, which stretches over an area of 742.38 ha (1,834.5 acres).
Q6064629: Çankırı Great Mosque, or Sultan Süleyman Mosque, dates from the era of Mimar Sinan. It was built by Sadık Kalfa on the orders of Suleiman the Magnificent.
Q14751553: İnandıktepe is an archaeological site located in Cankiri Province, Turkey, about 50 miles northeast of Ankara and 115 kilometers northwest of Hattusa.
Q6031100: The Independence Road (İstiklal Yolu) is the 344 km route from the coast at İnebolu through Kastamonu and Çankırı to Ankara. During the War of Independence, ammunition landed at İnebolu was carried along it to the front by ox carts. In 2018 an area of 2,357 decares was declared a national park.
Q85741449:
Anadynata was a town of ancient Paphlagonia, inhabited in Byzantine times. 
Its site is located near Kurşunlu, Asiatic Turkey.
Q98690921: Çankırı Museum is a museum in the province of Çankırı, Türkiye.
Q6048452: Ali Bey Mosque is a mosque in the Ali Bey quarter of central Çankırı. Its inscription shows it was built in 1609.
Q21527407: Çankırı Clock Tower stands in central Çankırı. The first clock tower on this spot was built in 1869; the present tower, put up in 1901, was moved to its current location in 1948.
